## Objective
The greeting A mark and the rendered-colour treatment **already ship**. The
owner-approved out-of-band UI baseline (AM-028, commit `b366be1`, an ancestor of
this card's base) created `BrandMark.tsx` and `BrandWordmark.tsx`, added the
`--brand-mark` token, and put the mark above the home greeting
(`HomeLauncher.tsx:71-73`) — so the headline deliverable this card was written
for is in the tree and is already unit-pinned by P2.1's approved tests. This
card is the reconciliation AM-028 owed P2.2
(`docs/v2/state/AMENDMENTS.md:33`, "Reconciliation owed"), and its deliverable
is coverage, not implementation: a real-browser spec that reads the two brand
colours as they are actually **painted** — in both themes, with the default
accent and with a non-default one — plus a real, falsifiable layout check at
200% zoom, and a unit test for the mark's placement on the home screen, so a
regression is a failing test rather than a quiet visual change. The
implementation shipped; the tests are the deliverable.

## Fixed decisions
The shipped brand implementation is already correct and this card changes none
of it. The already-shipped behaviour these tests must pin, read off the base
commit:

- **The greeting A mark, as the home screen renders it**
  (`HomeLauncher.tsx:69-76`): `BrandMark` is the **first child of
  `.home-inner`** and a **sibling** of the `h1` — never inside it, because it
  is decorative and the heading's whole text stays `Let’s focus on…`. It is
  centred (`BrandMark.tsx:23,25`: `display: block`, `margin: 0 auto`) and
  **48 px** tall (`:24`), `aria-hidden="true"` and `focusable="false"`
  (`:19-20`). That is A4.
- **Two elements, two colour rules — the top-bar wordmark is not
  `--brand-mark`.** The A mark is `color: var(--brand-mark)`
  (`BrandMark.tsx:22`) ⇒ **`rgb(31, 111, 99)`** in light (`tokens.css:183`) and
  **`rgb(255, 255, 255)`** in dark (`:332`). The wordmark is rendered
  `tone="text"` at **both** call sites (`TopBar.tsx:25`,
  `PatientsColumn.tsx:100`), which `BrandWordmark.tsx:37` resolves to
  `color: var(--text-primary)` ⇒ **`rgb(38, 38, 32)`** in light
  (`tokens.css:109`) and **`rgb(240, 238, 230)`** in dark (`:310`). Both
  tokens are literal hex, so both are **accent-invariant**: changing the accent
  must not move either of them.
- **D10's wording predates the owner's placement choice, and the code wins.**
  `DECISIONS.md:24` still reads "Wordmark and A mark: `#1f6f63` in light mode,
  `#ffffff` in dark mode", which described the `--brand-mark` token before the
  2026-09-26 preview put the top bar's word in the foreground colour
  (`BrandWordmark.tsx:8-12`, `TopBar.tsx:19-24`, authorised by AM-028). This
  card pins the values above and does **not** edit `DECISIONS.md`. Do not "fix"
  either surface back to `var(--brand-mark)` or change the wordmark back to
  D10's colour: that is a revert of an owner-approved baseline, and a stop
  condition below. Re-wording D10 is a separate amendment for the coordinator,
  not this card's work.
- **`data-theme` on `<html>` is the resolved theme, never the literal
  `system`** (`appearance.ts:71`, `resolveTheme` at `:85-87`). After asking for
  a theme through the API, assert `data-theme` equals `light` or `dark` before
  reading any colour, exactly as `settings-appearance.spec.ts:38,88,117` does.
  Under Playwright's light-OS emulation `system` resolves to `light`.
- **Theme and accent are server settings, so the only deterministic way to set
  them is `request.put('/api/settings', { data: … })`**
  (`appearance.ts:23-24`): `{ theme: 'light' | 'dark' }` and
  `{ accent_color: '#7c3aed' }`. There is no client-only path, and the Settings
  UI is a client path over the same row — use the API, as
  `settings-appearance.spec.ts:26,75` does. That row is **global to the run**:
  one server, one database, `fullyParallel: true` (`playwright.config.ts:45`).
- **The non-default accent is `#7c3aed`.** `DEFAULT_ACCENT_COLOR` is `#1f6f63`
  (`settings.ts:36`), byte-identical to `--brand-mark` light
  (`tokens.css:183`), so a near-teal pick would prove nothing. The two
  "default accent" states must **PUT `#1f6f63` explicitly** rather than leave
  the accent unset, so the state does not depend on what a sibling spec left
  behind; the claim is then between `#1f6f63` and `#7c3aed`. In the two
  non-default states, first assert the root's `--accent` really changed — read
  it with `getComputedStyle(...).getPropertyValue('--accent').trim()` and
  **record the string**, which the engine may serialise as the literal or as
  `rgb(124, 58, 237)` — then assert **both** brand colours are byte-identical
  to the values the default-accent run saw. That invariance is the point of the
  accent column: it is what catches `--brand-mark` or `--text-primary` being
  re-derived from `--accent`.
- **The A mark is selected by its viewBox, scoped to the home screen:**
  `page.getByTestId('home').locator('svg[viewBox="0 0 562 754"]')` — one
  element whether or not the listbox is open, because every `StrokeIcon` is
  `viewBox="0 0 24 24"` (`icons.tsx:18`) and the "New" row puts one inside
  `.home` whenever a search is typed (`HomeLauncher.tsx:135`). It is the same
  value P2.1's `BrandMark.test.tsx:58` pins, so the e2e and the unit test
  cannot drift apart. **No `data-testid` is added to the mark**:
  `BrandMark.tsx:10-12` takes only `className` and it is not editable. The
  wordmark's handle is the existing `page.getByRole('img', { name: 'Apunta' })`
  (`BrandWordmark.tsx:33-34`, pinned by `TopBar.test.tsx:46-48`); on `/`
  exactly one element answers, so assert the count is 1 before reading a
  colour.
- **The 200% zoom check is a real, falsifiable layout check.** The old wording
  — "the wordmark does not overlap the next top-bar item" — had nothing to
  check: in the standalone bar the wordmark is the only child
  (`TopBar.tsx:17-27`), and in the sidebar's bar the panel toggle is to its
  **left** and the wordmark is last (`PatientsColumn.tsx:82-101`). What *is*
  assertable at 200% zoom, and is what these tests must pin: the wordmark's box
  and `[data-testid="sidebar-toggle"]`'s box **do not intersect**; the
  wordmark's box stays **inside** its bar's box; and on the home screen the A
  mark's box is 48 px tall, horizontally **centred** in `.home-inner` (a ±1 px
  tolerance on the centre offset), and clear of `[data-testid="home-search"]`.
  Two facts make the check possible at all. 200% zoom is not a Playwright
  primitive, so model it the way Chromium models it — the CSS layout viewport
  halves and the device pixel ratio doubles — with `page.setViewportSize()` at
  half the window, or a CDP `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` carrying
  `deviceScaleFactor: 2`; **record which you used and the numbers you
  measured.** And the window must be **at least 1800 px wide**: halving the
  default 1280×720 viewport lands at 640 px, below the `max-width: 900px`
  breakpoint (`app.css:3588-3599`), where every column but the active pane is
  `display: none`, the home greeting has no box to measure, and
  `boundingBox()` returns null. The spec must assert the home screen is still
  visible *after* the zoom is applied, so that trap fails loudly instead of
  silently.
- **No patient data anywhere in this card.** The unit test renders
  `HomeLauncher` with `patients={[]}` and a `vi.fn()` `onSelect`; the e2e seeds
  exactly one note format named `uniqueName('E2E brand format')` (fabricated,
  HS-8). No patient, no note, no transcript.
- **No production change.** If honouring an assertion seems to need an edit to
  any file in Must not edit, that is a stop, not a task.

   `screen.queryByRole('img')` is null); and the inline 48 px height and

   second thing to keep in step. Run `npm run build:shared && npx vitest run
   web/src/components/HomeLauncher.test.tsx` and record the result **as
   observed**.
2. Add `e2e/tests/brand.spec.ts`, importing `test`, `expect` and `uniqueName`
   from `../support/fixtures` (not from `@playwright/test`, so the auto
   console-error fixture at `fixtures.ts:9-25` is inherited and a React key
   warning is reported as what it is). One `test.describe('brand …')` with
   `test.describe.configure({ mode: 'serial' })` — the four appearance states
   write one global settings row, so they must not run concurrently under
   `fullyParallel`. In `beforeAll`, `GET /api/settings` and keep the current
   `theme` and `accent_color`; in `afterAll` `request.put('/api/settings', …)`
   them back, and record the observed and restored values as evidence. The
   sandbox data directory is per-run, so the blast radius is one Playwright
   run and never the owner's data (HS-1).
3. Inside each test, reach the home screen deterministically and set the state
   before reading anything: `request.post('/api/formats', { data: { name:
   uniqueName('E2E brand format'), sections: ['Subjective', 'Plan'] } })` — a
   database with no format redirects `/` to `/onboarding/format`
   (`Workspace.tsx:323-324`), so there is no `data-testid="home"` at all — then
   `request.put('/api/settings', …)` for the theme and accent, then
   `page.goto('/')`, `await expect(page.getByTestId('home')).toBeVisible()`,
   `await expect(page.locator('html')).toHaveAttribute('data-theme', theme)`,
   and only then `getComputedStyle` on the A mark and on the wordmark. Assert
   the wordmark handle resolves to exactly one element first.
4. Write **four colour tests, one per state, each titled with its state and its
   expected pair** so the run's own list output is the evidence, and each
   asserting both elements: `brand: light, default accent #1f6f63 — A mark
   rgb(31, 111, 99), wordmark rgb(38, 38, 32)`, the same pair again for
   `light, accent #7c3aed`, `brand: dark, default accent #1f6f63 — A mark
   rgb(255, 255, 255), wordmark rgb(240, 238, 230)`, and the same pair again
   for `dark, accent #7c3aed`. Every title starts with `brand:`, which is what
   V1's `--grep "brand"` matches.
5. Write the zoom test, `brand: at 200% zoom the wordmark and the sidebar
   toggle do not overlap, and the A mark is 48px and centred`: widen the window
   to at least 1800 px, apply the zoom model Fixed decisions names, re-assert
   the home screen is visible, then the boxes. Compare boxes by geometry
   (`boundingBox()`), not by eyeballing a screenshot: no intersection between
   the wordmark and the toggle, wordmark inside its bar, mark 48 px, centre
   offset within ±1 px of `.home-inner`'s centre, mark clear of
   `home-search`.
6. Screenshots: each colour test writes one PNG into
   `docs/v2/evidence/P2.2/screenshots/`, with the path anchored to the
   repository root — `resolve(import.meta.dirname, '..', '..', 'docs/v2/evidence/P2.2/screenshots', <name>.png)`
   — **not** a relative path, because `npm run e2e --workspace @apunta/e2e`
   runs Playwright with cwd `e2e/`, so a relative path would land in
   `e2e/docs/…`. `e2e/screenshots/` and `e2e/test-results/` are disposable run

   the evidence folder: `<sandbox>` for sandbox paths, `~` for the home folder,
   no hostnames, usernames or real names. With one fabricated format and two
   settings values, no patient data is on screen (HS-8).
7. Record what each run actually printed, including a first run that passes
   unchanged: this behaviour already exists, so a pass on the base commit is the
   expected outcome and is the evidence, not a missing failure. Leave the change
   uncommitted for the coordinator.

## Stop conditions
- A new test shows the shipped behaviour does **not** match Fixed decisions — a
  rendered colour that is not the pinned pair for its element and theme, a mark
  that follows `--accent`, a mark that is not 48 px or not centred, a mark that
  is inside the `h1`, a wordmark that intersects its neighbour at 200% zoom:
  report it as a finding for the coordinator and **do not** change the file to
  make the test pass. Record the failing assertion, the observed value and the
  source line. `HomeLauncher.tsx` is in May edit in no version of this card.
- Honouring a Fixed decision would change the owner-approved AM-028 treatment —

# Run configuration (v2 plan)

## 1. Ports

| Use | Port |
| --- | --- |
| Live instance: **never contact** | 7717 |
| Sandbox servers (C-ISO) | 7800 to 7889 |
| Updater test server (C-UPD) | 7890 to 7899 |
| Playwright under the sandbox | the port `sandbox.mjs env` assigns |

## 2. Gate levels

A card names one level. Commands run from the repository root unless a card
says otherwise. Until P0.3 is APPROVED, only L0 and the non-launching part of
L1 may run.

| Level | When | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **L0** docs only | cards that change only Markdown | `npx prettier --check <changed files>`; `node scripts/check-no-external-urls.mjs` |
| **L1** targeted | every implementation card | `npm run lint`; `npm run typecheck`; `npm run build:shared`, then the card's named test files with `npx vitest run <paths>` from the repository root (the root `vitest.config.ts` defines the projects) |
| **L2** parent acceptance | every parent review card | everything in §3 |
| **L3** native or real model | cards and parent reviews that say so | the card's listed commands, all through `sandbox.mjs` |

## 3. The L2 suite

```sh
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
TZ=UTC npm test
TZ=America/Denver npm test
TZ=America/Mexico_City npm test
TZ=Australia/Sydney npm test
npm run build
node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs env --port 7810 > /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && . /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && npm run e2e
npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1
```

After P0.2, each `TZ=` run prints its effective zone (a test asserts it), so
four runs really exercise four zones. After P0.3, the e2e line is the only
permitted way to run Playwright. After S3.2, add
`npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1 --corpus e2e/fixtures/eval-es/tuning`.
After P3.3, add `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and
`cargo test` in `src-tauri/`.

## 4. Evidence

- Write detailed output to `docs/v2/evidence/<card-id>/`. Keep it sanitized:
  replace sandbox paths with `<sandbox>`, the home folder with `~`, and never
  include hostnames, usernames, keys, tokens or real names.
- Raw logs stay in the sandbox run folder and are never committed.
- Each command's evidence records: working directory, exact command, exit
  code, start and end time, and a short excerpt (failures in full, up to 200
  lines).
- Status words: criteria `NOT RUN`, `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`; cards
  `NOT STARTED`, `IN PROGRESS`, `SUBMITTED`, `APPROVED`,
  `CHANGES REQUESTED`, `BLOCKED`; instruction reviews `CLEAR`, `DEFECT`,
  `UNKNOWN`. Every blank template starts at `NOT RUN` or `UNKNOWN`.
